cases.title: Stereographic Spherical Sliced Wasserstein Distances
cases.study_claim: The stereographic distance is well-defined under the published spherical moment condition.
cases.observation: Theorem 3.2 requires transformed moments: finite spherical moments do not ensure finite stereographic Wasserstein distance.
cases.consequence: We withdrew the antipodal example. With infinite support, projection can still yield an infinite distance.
cases.location: Theorem 3.2 and Appendix Theorem D.3.
evidence: Set d=2, p=1, h=id and weights w_n=6/(pi^2*n^2).
Points s_n=(4*n^2/(n^4+4),0,(n^4-4)/(n^4+4)) lie in S2 minus the north pole.
Their stereographic images are (n^2,0).
The probability measure sum w_n delta_s_n has finite spherical first moment.
Its projected first moment diverges, since every atom contributes 6/pi^2.
Almost every directional W1 distance to the south-pole Dirac is infinite.
limits: The old antipodal-Dirac argument was wrong and is explicitly retracted.
The correct rotationally averaged antipodal distance is pi*sqrt(2), not infinity.
The replacement uses an infinite-support measure approaching the excluded pole.
Finite empirical data and bounded/capped implementations are not refuted.
